claim: The decisive eighteenth-century European reordering around South Asia was not a single eight-year war: the War of the Austrian Succession opened a long Anglo-French contest in India, while the Seven Years War destroyed the French ability to compete with the East India Company as a comparable territorial power.
bounded_by: Three distinct scholarly works support the sequence but all are currently registered through the Cambridge publishing domain. Retain the strategic-asymmetry conclusion as bounded same-publisher corroboration until an independent source family is added; French commercial presence is not treated as disappearing after 1763.
notes: French trading posts survived/reappeared after 1763; the change is strategic asymmetry, not French disappearance.
